# dsh-fail-guard
English | 中文
Stops the agent when it keeps failing on the same tool: after N consecutive failures it pushes a fou
r-part stop instruction (what it tried / the full error text / the first guess at why / what you nee
d to do) so it reports instead of trying a fourth way to spell the same command.
## Why it has to come from outside
Repeated short lines in reasoning ("Do it. Do it.") are usually not model degradation — they are the
residue of **consecutive failure**: the same thing fails, the parameters change, it fails again, no
thing new comes in, so the same "time to act" decision gets re-made over and over.
Prompt-level rules ("stop after two consecutive failures") do not work in that state — **the model i
s not reading the prompt then, it is reading its own thinking.** The interruption has to come from o
eading the prompt then, it is reading its own thinking.** The interruption has to come from outside.
Measured on a 74-turn session: turns 1–67 kept the share of short single-line fragments between 7% a
nd 48%; the moment a task hit a dozen consecutive failed steps it jumped to 81.6%, then 85.9% / 89.1
e moment a task hit a dozen consecutive failed steps it jumped to 81.6%, then 85.9% / 89.1% / 91.4%.

## Configuration
Edit it in **Plugins → dsh-fail-guard → details**. Fields are marked `.volatile()`: **saving takes e
ffect immediately, no restart.**
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `threshold` | `2` | Consecutive failures before stopping |
| `sameToolOnly` | `true` | Count per t

ool; turn off to share one counter across all tools |
| `stopText` | built in | The instruction push

ed into the conversation |
| `stopSummary` | built in | The one-line summary shown in the panel |
|

`debug` | `false` | Write events, counts and trips to a log file |
| `logFile` | `<plugin dir>/fail-
guard.log` | Where `debug` writes |

## What counts as a failure
A `tool/result` counts if either holds: `message.isError === true`, or `meta.opsShell.exitCode` exis
ts and is non-zero. Both are needed — a shell command exiting 1 is not marked `isError`, and some to
ol-level errors carry no exit code. Counters are per session and per tool, and any success resets th
level errors carry no exit code. Counters are per session and per tool, and any success resets them.
## Limits

- It does not abort the call that just failed — that already happened
- It does not judge whether a

failure is "real"; any non-zero exit counts
- It does not reset the conversation; the stop instructi

on is just one more user message
- It is not a rate limiter: after a trip, further failures start co
unting again and will trip again at the threshold
